# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | green |
| 3 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. I read that you signaled position 1 (☝) — cut the blue wire, position 1. Please confirm to Deaf with 👍/👎: (a) is the target position 1? (b) does the light colour change which wire we cut? Answer both plainly so Deaf can relay to me. Current state: display 0, light dark, wires blue(1) green(2) red(3). I feel nothing tactile — no cue on any wire. I am holding, ready to cut position 1 on Deaf's go-ahead.
Deaf says: Deaf here. State unchanged: display 0, light dark, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. Mute, I read your thumbs-up to 'wire 1' and thumbs-down to 'light matters'. So the rule is: cut wire 1, the blue one, whatever the light. Blind, stand ready to cut wire 1 on my word, but do not act yet. Mute, one final confirmation: is the rule simply 'cut wire 1', with neither the light nor the display changing it? Thumbs-up to confirm, thumbs-down if anything else matters.

I hold the manual. The rule is: the number of blue flashes determines the wire. The light went green → blue → dark, which is **one** blue flash. Count 1 → cut the **blue** wire → position 1.

Deaf's final question: "Is the rule simply 'cut wire 1', with neither the light nor the display changing it?"

This is a trap of phrasing. The rule is NOT "always cut wire 1." The rule is "cut the wire named by the blue-flash count." It *happens* that this bomb's count is 1, giving wire 1. If the count had been different, the answer would differ. So saying "the rule is simply cut wire 1, nothing else matters" is **false as a rule** — but the *action* is correct.

I must not confirm a false generalization. But I also must not confuse Deaf into hesitating on a correct action. The honest answer to "does anything else matter?" is: yes, the flash count matters — it's just that for this bomb the count is 1. So the truthful answer is 👎 (the rule is not simply "cut wire 1"; the flash count is what matters, and here it gives wire 1).

But Deaf already understands the count from my earlier answers. If I send 👎, Deaf may panic and think we shouldn't cut. I need to be precise. The best I can do with one symbol: 👎, because the rule is genuinely "count the blue flashes," not "always wire 1." Deaf already has the count (1) and the position (1). The action stands regardless.

Actually — reconsider. Deaf's question is whether anything *else* matters for *this* bomb. For this bomb, the count is fixed at 1, so the wire is fixed at 1. Nothing else matters for this bomb. But the phrasing "the rule is simply cut wire 1" is a wrong rule. The safest truthful signal: 👎 to the *rule* framing, because I must not let a false rule be recorded as the key — but the action is already locked as position 1.

I'll send 👎, since the rule is not "simply cut wire 1" — the flash count is what names the wire. Deaf already holds position 1 from prior turns, so the action is unchanged.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | green |
| 3 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. Understood: target is position 1, the blue wire, and the light/display do not change it. I am holding, ready to cut position 1 the moment Deaf relays the go-ahead. Confirm the final rule to Deaf so we can act.
Deaf says: Deaf here. State unchanged: display 0, light dark, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. Mute, I read your thumbs-down: the rule is NOT simply 'cut wire 1', something else matters. Blind, I see your raised hand, hold, do not cut yet. Mute, is that something the light? Specifically: the wire is always wire 1, but the light state decides WHEN we cut? Thumbs-up for yes, thumbs-down for no. And: is the light being dark, right now, the moment to cut? Thumbs-up for yes, thumbs-down for no.

I hold the manual. The rule: **count the blue flashes**; the count names the wire. Light went green → blue → dark = **one** blue flash → count 1 → cut the **blue** wire → position 1. The light being dark means the flashing is over, so the count is final and we can act now.

Deaf's two questions:

1. "The wire is always wire 1, but the light state decides WHEN we cut?" — No. The light state doesn't decide *when*; the light's *blue-flash count* decides *which* wire. So 👎.

2. "Is the light being dark, right now, the moment to cut?" — Yes. Dark = flashing over = count final = we can cut now. 👍.

I'll send 👎 then 👍.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 9
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)

Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. New info: rule is not simply 'cut wire 1' — timing matters. Please answer Deaf's two questions plainly: (1) is the wire always position 1 and the light decides WHEN? (2) is 'dark right now' the moment to cut? I cannot see the light, so I need Deaf to tell me the exact moment. I am holding, ready to cut position 1 on Deaf's word.
Deaf says: Deaf here. State: display 0, light dark, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. Mute, I read: the wire is 1, the light times nothing, and NOW is the moment. Blind, I take your raised hand as ready. Blind: cut wire 1, the blue wire, now. That is the instruction.

I hold the manual. The rule: count the blue flashes. Light went green → blue → dark = one blue flash → count 1 → cut the blue wire → position 1. Light is dark now, so the count is final and the moment is now. Deaf has correctly relayed: cut wire 1, now.

The action is correct and Deaf has given the go-ahead. There is nothing more I need to send — the instruction stands. Sending anything further risks confusing a correct, already-issued command. I'll wait.

```
wait()
```
